text: Yes, the 2022 loss was detected using Sentinel-2 imagery. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13), which relies on Landsat and Sentinel-2 data, confirmed tree-cover loss in 2022 covering 0.6 ha of the asset. The JRC 2020 reference dataset corroborated this event, validating the loss. Additionally, the MGAP 2021 forest map identified the affected area as native forest, supporting the detection. While there were smaller loss patches (0.2 ha) under 0.5 ha in 2022, the primary event was conclusively observed.
